title: SIEM onboarding: field mappings, RBAC v2 checklist, and evidence automation
body:
Purpose:
This working doc captures the checklist and concrete field-mapping guidance for onboarding customers who want SIEM exports from Redwood Inference. It focuses on three vendor targets (Splunk HEC, Datadog Events/Logs API, Azure Sentinel/Log Analytics), plus recommended RBAC v2 mappings and evidence-automation expectations.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: Security engineers, SRE, customer SOC integrators, and Solutions Engineers.
- Scope: Export schema, mapping examples, RBAC implications, delivery and retry semantics, acceptance tests for onboarding. Not a full implementation guide for vendor SDKs.

Executive summary (short):
Customers expect consistent audit fields (tenant, user, request_id, model, model_version, prompt_hash, redaction_flags, latency_ms, outcome) regardless of SIEM backend. Connector must support per-tenant isolation, TLS + mTLS where requested, backpressure, batching, and idempotent delivery. RBAC v2 must map Redwood roles to customer SIEM user/actor fields so alerts can be correlated with auth context.

Checklist for customer scoping (quick):
- Confirm desired SIEM: Splunk HEC | Datadog Logs/Events | Sentinel (Log Analytics or Event Hub).
- Delivery method: push (HEC/Datadog) or pull (Event Hub / S3 / syslog).
- Throughput estimate: average requests/s and peak tokens/s per minute. (We need 95th percentile qps and average event size).
- Retention & PII policy: confirm whether prompts or outputs may contain PII; if yes, enable redaction hooks and evidence-only exports.
- RBAC mapping: provide list of customer groups and mapping rules to Redwood roles (admin, dev, svc, auditor).
- SLA for loss: acceptable risk (at most X events/hour dropped).

RBAC v2 mapping guidance (practical):
- Include these fields in every exported event: actor.id, actor.type (user|service|integration), actor.roles (comma-separated), auth_method (sso|token|api-key), auth_session_id.
- Map Redwood principals to customer names where requested via mapping table: e.g., redwood:alice@redwood -> acme:alice@acme. Provide mapping file or SCIM sync if customer requests automated sync.
- For canary/dedicated/private customers, include deployment_id and env tags.

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC string
- event_type: e.g., user.login, model.inference.request, model.inference.response, permission.change, policy.override
- request_id: uuid v4 (Redwood request id)
- correlation_id: client-provided id (optional)
- tenant_id: internal tenant uuid
- actor.id, actor.type, actor.roles
- resource.type: e.g., model, route, dataset
- resource.id: model_name or route_id
- model_name, model_version, quant_profile (if applicable)
- prompt_safe_hash: sha256(prompt) OR redacted_prompt if allowed
- response_safe_hash: sha256(response) when storing only fingerprints
- token_count_in, token_count_out, latency_ms
- outcome: success|error|timeout|fallback
- error.code, error.message (avoid PII in message)
- redaction_flags: list of fields redacted (prompt, response, user_message)
- evidence_refs: array of urls/ids for longer artifacts (S3, internal archive)

Field mapping examples to vendor payloads (short):
- Splunk HEC: map timestamp->time, event_type -> event.type, request_id -> event.request_id, include all canonical fields under event.fields.*. Use host=redwood-inference, source=redwood.audit. Set index based on customer mapping.
- Datadog Logs API: map timestamp to @timestamp, send attributes under dd.tags and attributes maps for token counts and model metadata. For security events, set service=redwood-inference and dd.source=redwood.audit.
- Sentinel/Log Analytics: send customLog table entries (Redwood_Audit_CL) with schema flattened: RequestId_s, TenantId_s, ActorId_s, EventType_s, Model_s, LatencyMs_d, Outcome_s.

Example event (canonical JSON for internal reference):
{
  "timestamp": "2024-09-12T18:23:12.123Z",
  "event_type": "model.inference.request",
  "request_id": "a3f6b2e4-8f56-4d2e-9c88-1fcb3b9f9a12",
  "tenant_id": "t-8a3b2c4d",
  "actor.id": "svc-redwood-ingest",
  "actor.type": "service",
  "actor.roles": "ingest,monitor",
  "resource.type": "model",
  "model_name": "redwood-3b-quantized",
  "model_version": "2024-08-10",
  "prompt_safe_hash": "sha256:4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904",
  "token_count_in": "42",
  "token_count_out": "128",
  "latency_ms": "312",
  "outcome": "success",
  "redaction_flags": "prompt",
  "evidence_refs": "s3://redwood-archive/tenants/t-8a3b2c4d/req/a3f6b2e4"
}

Vendor specific payload snippets (note: these are examples, include vendor-specific headers and auth in integration):
- Splunk HEC event body (send POST /services/collector/event):
{ "time": 1694548992.123, "event": { ...canonical event... }, "host": "redwood-inference", "index": "acme-tenant-audit" }

- Datadog Logs API (v1) payload example:
[{"ddsource": "redwood.audit", "service": "redwood-inference", "hostname": "api-1", "message": "model.inference.request", "timestamp": 1694548992123, "attributes": { ...canonical fields... } }]

- Sentinel (Log Analytics ingestion) flattened sample row:
RequestId_s="a3f6b2e4-8f56", TenantId_s="t-8a3b2c4d", EventType_s="model.inference.request", ActorId_s="svc-redwood-ingest", Model_s="redwood-3b-quantized"

Evidence automation flow (recommended):
1) Event exported with prompt_safe_hash only and evidence_refs for full payload stored in secure S3 bucket.
2) If customer requires richer evidence for investigation, create evidence bundle job that: grabs full prompt/response, scrubs PII based on config, stores to long-term archive, and attaches a signed URL in evidence_refs.
3) Automate evidence retention TTL by tenant (e.g., 90 days default, 365 days for enterprise) and include retention metadata on exported event.
4) Audit/search: provide a lightweight index (search token) that points to evidence_refs without sending full text to SIEM unless customer opts in.

Operational requirements for connectors (must-have):
- TLS 1.2+ and support for mTLS when requested.
- Backpressure: buffer with bounded queue (configurable per-tenant) and circuit-breaker that emits a special audit event when buffer is full.
- Batching: group up to N events or max M bytes or max T seconds before flush. Defaults: N=100, M=1MB, T=5s.
- Idempotency: use request_id as idempotency key for consumer endpoints that support it.
- Retry semantics: retry with exponential backoff for 5xx; do not retry on 4xx except 429. For 429 include Retry-After handling.
- Observability: per-tenant metrics for success_rate, avg_latency, queued_events, dropped_events, last_delivery_error.
- Access control: only allow connector config changes to users with admin role in RBAC v2.

Acceptance criteria for customer onboarding (minimal):
- Test vector suite (provided by Redwood) shows canonical events arrive in customer's SIEM with correct fields (tenant_id, request_id, actor.id) and timestamps within 2s of source time for push integrations.
- Evidence refs are resolvable by Redwood SRE within expected ACLs.
- Failure mode test: agent simulates endpoint downtime; Redwood connector must emit a 'redwood.siem.delivery.failure' event to a separate monitoring index and not silently drop more than allowed threshold.

Privacy & PII notes (mandatory):
- Default: redact prompt/response content and send only hashes.
- If customer signs explicit data-sharing addendum, allow full-text exports with explicit per-tenant toggles and audit trail for opt-in.

Tests & onboarding runbook (short):
1) Solutions engineer collects customer endpoints, auth secrets, index/table mapping, and throughput estimate.
2) Set up staging connector with test token and run the 10-event smoke test (1 login, 3 model requests, 1 fallback, 5 policy changes).
3) Verify field presence in SIEM, then run 1k events at expected 95th percentile qps to validate backpressure and batching.
4) Review RBAC mappings and SCIM/Mapping file.
5) Sign-off: customer SOC confirms event fidelity and retention policy.

Open questions for the team (to resolve in follow-up):
- Do we expose an official SCIM endpoint for mapping Redwood principals into customer tenant directories?
- How to best version the export schema (semantic versioning header?) so customers can detect breaking changes? Proposal: add header X-Redwood-Schema: audit.v1.2

Next steps (action items):
- Marco: prototype Splunk HEC staging connector that supports mTLS and batching (ETA: 2024-10-04).
- Evelyn: produce a compact onboarding test suite (json payloads + validator queries) (ETA: 2024-09-20).
- Samir: draft data-sharing addendum clause and retention defaults for legal review (ETA: 2024-09-25).

Notes to self / working achecks:
- Keep example payloads intentionally conservative (avoid real PII).
- Preserve ability to flip between hash-only evidence and full-text evidence per-tenant.
